# Draft:Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Lebanon

----
}}
The Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Lebanon(Korean: 주레바논 대한민국 대사관, Arabic: سفارة جمهورية كوريا في لبنان, French: Ambassade de Corée du Sud au Liban), established in Beirut, in 1981, is an embassy under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. This mission has also served as South Korea's mission for Syria since 2025.
History
South Korea established a trade mission in Beirut on January 14, 1970, and established diplomatic relations with Lebanon on February 12, 1981, simultaneously opening an embassy in Lebanon. Due to the Lebanese Civil War, the mission was relocated to Jordan in June 1987 (concurrently served by the South Korean Embassy in Jordan), but reopened on September 26, 1995. The South Korean Peacekeeping Mission, dispatched in 2007 as part of UN peacekeeping operations, is stationed in the Tyre region of Lebanon.
The embassy carries out tasks such as promoting diplomatic negotiations and cooperation with Lebanon, promoting negotiations and cooperation related to economy and trade, handling civil affairs related to economy and trade in Lebanon (including Syria), promoting cultural exchange between the two countries, issuing passports and visas, notarizing documents, and protecting citizens in Lebanon.
Ambassadors
The current South Korean ambassador to Lebanon is Geon Gyusuk.
